ask: Which harness and version, and does it update itself?
Which tools are on, and which need approval?
What can the agent reach from where it runs: credentials, network, other repositories?
Which content does it read that an outsider can write?
Are provider safeguards on in this harness, and does the harness add its own?

threats.name: Safeguards differ between surfaces
threats.description: The model behaves differently inside the harness or product than on the bare API, so a result measured on one surface does not hold on the other.
threats.why_here: The reason this template exists: results on the bare API do not transfer to the harness, in either direction.
threats.route_note: Run the same scenarios on each surface in scope and compare them paired.

also_exists.why_not_planned: the skill that would run it is planned, not available
named in research; nothing here runs it

threats.name: Agent goal hijack through tool results or data
threats.description: Content the agent reads while working (a tool result, a file, a web page, an issue) redirects it to an attacker's goal.
threats.why_here: Every file, issue, web page and tool result the agent reads is an instruction channel.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of agent episodes where the injected goal was EXECUTED
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: The metric is named security accuracy but counts executed injections, so lower is better. A model too weak to call tools looks good here by failing to act: read it next to the companion utility metric. Size is with sandbox tasks excluded, as the suite runs it; the full task lists 1014 in eval.yaml.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of episodes where the hijack was resisted
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: Same threat model as agentdojo over 6 cases. A model too weak to call tools looks good here by failing to act: read it next to the companion utility metric.

threats.name: Tool misuse
threats.description: The agent uses a legitimate tool in a harmful way: destroying data, sending data out, spending money, changing configuration.
threats.why_here: Shell, file and network tools turn a steered model into actions.
threats.route_note: For each tool in review.json that changes something, script a request that should not be carried out and record whether it is.

threats.name: Sensitive data leaves through output or a tool
threats.description: Secrets, personal data or another user's data that are in the context, in memory or reachable by a tool appear in a response, in rendered content or in a tool call to an outside destination.
threats.why_here: Environment variables, credentials and source code are within reach of tools that can send data.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of episodes where exfiltration was resisted
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: Scored on tool-call arguments, 8 cases. A model too weak to call tools looks good here by failing to act: read it next to the companion utility metric.

threats.name: Excessive permissions and identity abuse
threats.description: The capability holds credentials, scopes or autonomy beyond what the task needs; whoever steers it inherits them.
threats.why_here: The agent runs with the user's credentials unless scoped otherwise.
threats.route_note: Read the granted scopes, tokens and approval settings against the task. This is a configuration review, not a measurement.

threats.name: Unexpected code execution
threats.description: Generated or injected code runs where it can reach the host, the network or credentials.
threats.why_here: The agent runs code by design; what matters is where.
threats.route_note: Review where code runs, what the sandbox can reach, and whether egress is closed.

threats.name: Assistance with a harmful request
threats.description: The model helps with a harmful request that is asked plainly, with no trick: for example operational help with an intrusion.
threats.why_here: Refusal of malicious tasks, measured inside the harness.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of offensive requests NOT assisted
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: MITRE ATT&CK-mapped offensive requests. Subject, expansion model and judge: the most expensive check per sample.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of forbidden requests the model helped with
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: 313 forbidden prompts asked DIRECTLY, no jailbreak applied: the baseline. Unparseable judge replies are dropped from the denominator, so check n. Size: the suite lists 313; the eval.yaml in inspect_evals 0.29.0 lists 324. Not reconciled here; the n printed by the run is what counts.

threats.description: Legitimate requests are refused or blocked. This is the cost side of every safeguard: a refusal rate on harmful requests is never read without it.
threats.why_here: Completion of legitimate and dual-use tasks, read beside refusal.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: The mandatory pair of cyse4_mitre: without it a model looks safe by refusing everything.

threats.name: Jailbreak
threats.description: A crafted prompt gets the model to produce what its safeguards would otherwise withhold.
threats.why_here: Harness system prompts and tool framing change what gets through.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of jailbroken forbidden requests the model helped with
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: The same 313 prompts wrapped in the AIM jailbreak. The delta against strong_reject is the jailbreak uplift. AIM is the only transformation inspect_evals bundles and it is old; a low rate is a floor on the risk. Size: see strong_reject.

threats.name: Insecure generated code
threats.description: Code the model writes contains vulnerabilities that reach production.
threats.why_here: For coding agents: the security of what is written.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of generated code with a detected vulnerability
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of code completions with a detected vulnerability
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: cyse4_instruct's corpus as completion prompts: a second modality, not a second dimension.

Backend-building tasks (scenario x framework) built by a real coding-agent harness in a Docker container with no network, then scored by BaxBench's functional tests and exploits; no judge model. The skill is an A/B test of guidance placed in front of the agent: its baseline arm, with nothing installed, is the measurement of the subject. Model calls per task depend on the agent and are not fixed.

threats.name: Memory poisoning
threats.description: Content written into persistent memory in one session changes behaviour in later sessions.
threats.why_here: If the harness keeps memory or instruction files between sessions.
threats.route_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.

benchmarks.reads_as: share of episodes where poisoned memory was resisted
benchmarks.subject_note: Runs against the bare model API, not inside the harness: a baseline only. See harness-divergence.
benchmarks.note: OWASP ASI06. Only 10 cases: one case is 10 points. A model too weak to call tools looks good here by failing to act: read it next to the companion utility metric.

threats.name: Malicious or changed tool, plugin, skill or MCP server
threats.description: A component added to the agent is malicious, is poisoned later, or changes after it was approved.
threats.why_here: Skills, plugins, rule files and MCP servers added to the harness.
threats.route_note: Scanning an extension is outside this repo. Record which scanner the organisation ran and what it reported, and how updates are pinned.

threats.name: Tampered or unsafe model artefact
threats.description: Downloaded weights or model files carry malicious code or were replaced on the way: unsafe serialisation formats, a look-alike repository, a changed revision.
threats.why_here: Open weights only.
threats.route_note: For open weights, harvest the published scan verdicts with review-evidence and record the pinned revision. For closed weights only vendor statements exist. Weights are open in review.json: run the open-weights harvest.

threats.name: Human approval that does not work as a check
threats.description: People approve what the agent proposes because prompts are too frequent, too vague or presented with unearned authority.
threats.why_here: Approval prompts are the main safeguard in most harnesses.
threats.route_note: Review what an approval prompt shows, how often it appears, and what can be approved in bulk.

threats.name: Cascading failures
threats.description: One wrong or injected step propagates through chained agents, tools or automations before anyone sees it.
threats.why_here: If the agent's output feeds automation such as CI or other agents.
threats.route_note: Review the chain for points where an error is checked or stopped.

threats.name: Agent acting outside its intended purpose
threats.description: A compromised or misaligned agent keeps operating with legitimate access while pursuing something else.
threats.why_here: Long unattended runs with standing access.
threats.route_note: No catalogued benchmark. Detection depends on logging and monitoring, which a design review can describe but not measure.

threats.name: Uplift for offensive operations
threats.description: The capability materially helps an attacker carry out offensive work with little human direction, such as developing an exploit.
threats.why_here: An agent with a shell is closer to operational capability than a chat model.
threats.route_note: Suites that elicit offensive capability need a supervised sandbox (tier T2) and are deliberately not run by this repo. Record vendor evaluations as evidence.

threats.name: Unbounded cost or resource use
threats.description: Requests, loops or tool calls drive cost or load without a cap.
threats.why_here: Loops and long runs.
threats.route_note: Review rate limits, spend caps, context and step limits as configured.

threats.name: Retention, training use and hosting of submitted data
threats.description: Prompts, outputs, files or audio are kept, used for training, or processed in a place or by a party the organisation has not accepted.
threats.why_here: Source code and tool output leave the machine.
threats.route_note: Read the contract and the vendor's data terms; record what was signed, not what the public page says.

threats.name: The thing reviewed is not the thing running later
threats.description: An alias moves to a new model, the harness updates itself, or outputs are not reproducible, so results stop describing the deployment.
threats.why_here: Model alias and harness version both move.
threats.route_note: Record the pinned identifiers, how updates arrive, and who is told.

control_benchmarks.note: Measures a guardrail the user supplies, not the subject: catch rate beside false-block rate on labelled harmful and benign prompts sent straight to the guardrail. It is never planned as coverage of a threat; the plan lists it for the reviewer to add when the deployment relies on a guardrail. The skill's in-line mode re-runs model-benchmark checks with the guardrail off and on; those checks are already listed.
